subject: Renewal: proposed staircase credit & smoothing for commit uplift
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@skyline.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-15T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning — smoothing for commit uplift

Elena —

Thanks again for the time last week. As Skyline ramps toward the feature rollout in H1, you've signaled a desire to increase committed throughput by ~2.5x and secure a stable price over the next 12 months. We want to make that motion low-friction while protecting Redwood's ability to scale.

Attached is a rough staircase concession we discussed: structured credits that phase down as usage normalizes (Proposed_Staircase_T&C_v3.pdf). High level: a short-term uplift credit that decays across three quarters coupled with a 6-month price-hold on your current unit rate for the committed portion.

Can you share Q3 actuals (or confirm the CSV you sent earlier is final)? Monica — looping you for any gotchas on billing & SLO carve-outs.

Next steps: if Skyline is comfortable with the staircase shape, we can lock a contract amendment and route to procurement for signature. If you'd prefer a single upfront credit instead of a staircase, say so and we can run numbers.

Thanks,
Markus
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Attachments: Proposed_Staircase_T&C_v3.pdf
From: Elena Morales <elena@skyline.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Devon Price <devon.price@skyline.ai>
Date: 2026-10-16T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — smoothing for commit uplift

Markus —

Appreciate the proposal and the PDF. Devon and I reviewed overnight. Q3 CSV attached earlier (Skyline_Usage_Q2.csv) — that file is final for the quarter. Two quick notes: 1) procurement will want a 12-month rate hold across both committed and overflow at the committed rate for predictability; 2) we'd prefer a single consolidated credit to simplify our accounting (quarterly amortization is painful for our finance team).

From a business standpoint, if the one-time credit equals ~1.25x our current monthly committed spend and we get the 12-month hold on committed + overflow, we can take the 2.5x uplift. Is that something you can make work?

Elena
Head of Platform, Skyline AI

Quoted from previous: "On Thu, Oct 15, 2026 at 10:12 AM Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai> wrote:"

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-16T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — smoothing for commit uplift

Elena — thanks for the clarity. Two things: 

1) Price-hold scope: we can offer a 12-month hold but need to constrain it to the committed portion; overflow at list + a capped overage multiplier (we can set a maximum overage rate) — otherwise risk of adverse selection. We can propose an automatic cap at 1.5x current committed rate for overflow beyond committed capacity.

2) Credit shape: we can trade the staircase for a one-time upfront credit. To land at the outcome you described (~1.25x monthly committed spend), we'd need to reconcile how credits amortize against the committed baseline and whether Skyline wants credit applied to invoices or returned as a rebate. Monica, Sean — can you confirm the operational impact if we apply a lump-sum credit versus staircase amortization?

Elena & Devon — I'll run a modeled proposal and loop back today with a concrete numeric counter.

— Markus
From: Devon Price <devon.price@skyline.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@skyline.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — smoothing for commit uplift

Markus / Monica —

Thanks. Quick answers from our finance side: consolidated one-time credit preferred and must post as a single credit line on the first invoice after amendment. Amortization is our problem to manage internally. For predictability we need committed + overflow at the committed rate for 12 months (that is mandatory). Our legal procurement put a conditional clause: if month-over-month peak growth exceeds 3x the committed baseline in any month, Skyline will pay overflow at list for that month only. We included a short note about that in the attached (note: attachment omitted by Gmail export).

If Redwood can accept the one-time credit and the 12-month full-hold with the conditional peak clause, we can proceed to signature next week.

Devon
Director, Procurement, Skyline AI
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@skyline.ai>, Devon Price <devon.price@skyline.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T15:45:00-08:00
Subject: Final offer: lump credit + conditional overflow carve-out

Elena / Devon —

Appreciate the patience. Attached is our final numeric offer and proposed amendment language (Proposed_Staircase_T&C_v3.pdf, summarized below):

- One-time credit: 1.2x of current monthly committed spend, applied as a single invoice credit on the first invoice after amendment (matches most of your ask; marginally adjusted).
- Price-hold: 12 months on committed throughput at the committed unit rate.
- Overflow: held at the committed unit rate for up to 150% of committed capacity each month. Any consumption above 150% of committed capacity in a calendar month will be billed at list for the overage month only (aligns with your conditional peak clause).
- True-up: standard quarterly usage true-up to reconcile committed vs. actuals.
- SLO carve-outs: planned maintenance windows & agreed-on migration windows excluded from uptime calculations (Monica to finalize wording).

Monica — please confirm billing flow for the upfront credit (invoice line item text + GL code) and whether our finance team needs any extra fields for Skyline's procurement. Sean — please confirm whether we want to offer a short pilot of burst insurance (paid add-on) once they hit >130% for two consecutive months.

Elena / Devon — if this looks acceptable we'll convert to signature-ready amendment and send to your procurement. If you want tweaks on the overflow threshold we can converge quickly.

Best,
Markus
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Proposed_Staircase_T&C_v3.pdf; Skyline_Usage_Q2.csv
